items.title: 68004_Howard McGhee oral history interview
items.q: And I had kind of changed a little bit from Louis to Roy, because I liked Roy and I liked what he was playing

ctx.x: Swing things mostly, you know. I mean, I was listening to Roy, too; I could hear him from Chicago. And I had kind of changed a little bit from Louis to Roy, because I liked Roy and I liked what he was playing -- because he was really playing in them days.

I'd never heard nobody else play like that except Charlie Jacobs. And Charlie, I couldn't hear him. He was out somewhere... Where he went, I don't know. But anyway, he went haywire, because after he found out that Harriet was gone he just went completely... He couldn't believe it, man. I said, "Well, she's gone. Just believe that, will you? You don't have to believe whether she loves you or not. Just believe that she ain't here no more. She's gone on out." But I'll tell you, when a man's in love, you can't talk…
